options.name: tensorfold_api_key
options.label: API key
options.doc: A key clients must send to use the engine's API, in addition to any keys in the key file. It is a secret and is never shown or logged. Changing it needs a restart and locks out clients using the old key.

options.name: tensorfold_close_ms
options.label: Shutdown grace period
options.doc: How long, in milliseconds, the engine may take to close in an orderly way when it is stopped (built-in 20,000). 0 skips the orderly close and ends connections at once. Keep it above the SSD cache's flush time.

options.name: tensorfold_grammar_lib
options.default_text: Beside the engine, then the system path
options.label: Tool-call grammar library
options.doc: The file path of the grammar library that constrains tool-call output. Unset, the engine looks beside itself and then on the system path. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tensorfold_log_polls
options.label: Log status polls
options.doc: Set to 1 to write an access line for every successful status poll (health, metrics and similar). Off by default because dashboards poll constantly and would flood the log; failed polls are always logged.

options.name: tensorfold_no_live
options.label: Plain console output
options.doc: Set to 1 to turn off the live status display drawn on a terminal and print ordinary log lines instead. Useful when output is captured or the terminal is not a real one.

options.name: tensorfold_no_update_check
options.label: Skip update check
options.doc: Accepted for compatibility with the earlier Python engine's setting. Nothing else in the code reads it, so it has no effect.

options.name: tensorfold_prepare_floor_gib
options.label: Free memory a request must leave
options.doc: The least free host memory, in GiB, a request's preparation (rendering and tokenizing its text) must leave (built-in 3). 0 turns the check off. A request that would breach it waits until memory frees up.

options.name: tensorfold_request_log
options.label: Request log file
options.doc: A file where every chat and completion request body is appended as one JSON line, images removed, so requests can be replayed later. Contains conversation text, so keep it private and switch it off when not needed.

options.name: tensorfold_seed_salt
options.label: Sampling seed salt
options.doc: A number mixed into the random seed the engine derives from the prompt when a request gives no seed (built-in 0). Changing it changes which sampled replies a prompt produces; a request's own seed is unaffected.

options.name: tf_grammar_dir
options.label: Grammar test: checkpoint folder
options.doc: Diagnostics: used only by the opt-in tool-grammar tests, which load a model checkpoint's tokenizer from this folder. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_grammar_stop
options.label: Grammar test: stop token
options.doc: Diagnostics: used only by the opt-in tool-grammar tests, to name the model's end-of-text token number. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_grammar_tokenizer
options.label: Grammar test: tokenizer file
options.doc: Diagnostics: used only by the opt-in grammar library test, which loads this tokenizer file. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_grammar_vocab
options.label: Grammar test: vocabulary size
options.doc: Diagnostics: used only by the opt-in grammar tests, to give the model's vocabulary width. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_sse_keepalive_s
options.label: Stream heartbeat interval
options.doc: How often, in seconds, a streaming reply sends a keep-alive when no tokens are flowing, so proxies do not drop an idle connection (built-in 15). 0 turns the heartbeats off.

options.name: tf_video_fps
options.label: Video frames per second
options.doc: How many frames per second are sampled from an uploaded video (built-in 2). Each frame is processed as an image, so more frames cost more prompt tokens and time.

options.name: tf_video_max_frames
options.label: Most video frames
options.doc: The most frames taken from one video (built-in 32); a longer clip's frames are spread evenly across it.

options.name: tf_video_max_side
options.label: Largest video frame side
options.doc: Each video frame is scaled down so neither side exceeds this many pixels (built-in 768, at least 32). Smaller frames cost fewer tokens but lose detail.

options.name: tensorfold_sse_keepalive
options.label: Base engine's stream heartbeat
options.doc: Whole seconds a stream may go without output (a long prompt's prefill) before it sends an SSE comment, so a client's idle timer does not drop it; 0, the default, never. It is the base engine's own heartbeat and runs beside the stream heartbeat interval setting, which is on by default.

options.name: tensorfold_plain_specials
options.label: Special-token text as plain text
options.doc: Set to 1 so special-token text that users, tools or search results wrote, or that a tool call carries, is ordinary text in the prompt. Off, every prompt is the template's text tokenized whole. It came with the base engine and has not been tested with this model.

options.name: tensorfold_libturbojpeg
options.label: JPEG library file
options.doc: The libturbojpeg file the engine loads to decode JPEG images. It must be libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1, so pixels match the reference decoder. Unset, the system's libturbojpeg is loaded; without one, JPEG images are refused and PNG images still work.

options.name: tensorfold_turbo_record
options.label: Turbo record file
options.doc: A file holding Turbo's measured record, which the admin page shows beside the Turbo switch. Unset or unreadable, the page shows the record built into the engine.
options.default_text: The record built into the engine

options.name: tensorfold_prefill_share
options.label: Prompt share beside decoding
options.doc: The share of wall time a long prompt's steps may take while other streams are generating, from 0.01 to 1 (default 1). At 1 the engine alternates one prompt step with one decode round; a lower share makes it run extra decode rounds after each prompt step, so generating streams slow down less and the prompt finishes later. Do not combine with the rounds-beside setting.

options.name: tf_ds_graphs
options.label: CUDA graphs for decode rounds
options.doc: Records the decode rounds' kernel launches as CUDA graphs and replays them, which cuts launch overhead. Costs device and host memory for each recorded graph (see the graph cap). Every server process must use the same value.

options.name: tf_ds_graph_cap
options.label: Most CUDA graphs kept
options.doc: The most recorded CUDA graphs kept; past it the least recently used are destroyed. 0 or unset keeps all of them, which grows over days as conversations lengthen and holds device and host memory on every node. Use the same number on every node.

options.name: tf_ds_pass_beside
options.label: Prompt pass size beside decoding
options.doc: The most rows a prompt pass may run while a stream is decoding, in whole 2,048-row units and no more than the prompt pass size. A smaller pass lets decode rounds in more often; a larger one finishes the prompt sooner.

options.name: tf_ds_pass_filling
options.label: Whole passes when prompts fill together

options.name: tf_ds_pass_tail
options.label: Merge a prompt's final pass
options.doc: Lets a prompt's final pass take the leftover rows after whole 2,048-row units, up to the pass size, instead of running the leftover as its own pass. Measured neutral from 4,000 to 19,000 tokens with equal replies; 0 runs the leftover separately.

options.name: tf_ds_pf_gemm5
options.label: Prompt dense GEMM at 5 stages
options.doc: Runs a prompt chunk's dense FP8 matrix multiplies that have no K split on a kernel with 5 loading stages instead of 3, so loads run further ahead. Same arithmetic in the same order, so replies are unchanged. Needs the model's own weights; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_pf_raster
options.label: Prompt GEMM grid grouping
options.doc: Makes large prompt matrix multiplies (activations of 14 MiB or more) walk their tile grid G row-tiles at a time (2, 4, 8 or 16) to reuse the GPU cache better. A speed experiment; any other value refuses the start. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_pf_tiles
options.label: Prompt tile kernels
options.doc: Prompt chunks use the tile kernels, which give the same bits as the older path. Set it to 0 to turn them off and fall back to the older kernels; several faster-prompt options need the tile kernels on.

options.name: tf_ds_prompt_max_wait_s
options.label: Longest prompt wait
options.doc: The longest any prompt waits for its next step, in whole seconds (1 to 86400), before it is taken next. A class in the prompt-priority table can set its own limit. Only matters when a prompt order or priority table is set.

options.name: tf_ds_prompt_order
options.label: Prompt step order
options.doc: How several prompts share the engine: 'serial' finishes one before the next, 'turns' alternates between them. Unset keeps the default rotation. Setting it also switches on the prompt priority and waiting limits.

options.name: tf_ds_prompt_qos
options.label: Prompt priority table
options.doc: A comma-separated list of size:class:overtakes[:max_wait_s] entries that gives prompts of each size range a class, how many other prompts it may overtake, and an optional longest wait. Unset leaves the order flat. A badly formed table refuses the start.

options.name: tf_ds_rounds_beside
options.default_text: Off (one prompt step, one decode round)
options.label: Decode rounds after each prompt step
options.doc: Runs this many decode rounds after every long prompt step while a stream is generating (twice as many after a paired step). It is a count-based alternative to the prompt share setting; setting both refuses the start.

options.name: tf_ds_round_rows
options.label: Most rows per round
options.doc: The most rows one decode round carries across all streams. It sizes the round's buffers, so a larger number uses more device memory. Every node must use the same value.

options.name: tf_ds_streams
options.label: Concurrent streams
options.doc: How many requests the engine generates for at once. Each stream holds its own window rings in device memory, so more streams use more memory. Every node must use the same value.

options.name: tf_ds_attn_u_decode
options.label: Decode attention from packed latents
options.doc: Makes a decode round's sparse attention read the packed latent values directly (the same arithmetic the prompt path uses) instead of unpacking them first. On by default (it does not change replies, and the decode half of TF_DS_ATTN_TWIN=z runs only in its calls; alone it measured x0.997 / x1.001, under the noise floor); 0 turns it off. A layer without the matching kernel keeps the normal one, and a kit without the extra set keeps the normal kernel with an 'off' line. Every server process must use the same setting.

options.name: tf_ds_conf_cal
options.label: Draft confidence calibration
options.doc: Two numbers written as a,b that turn the drafter's confidence into the chance a draft token is accepted (sigmoid of a times confidence plus b). The built-in 1,0.19 comes from a fit of 399 logged rounds on this cluster. Leave it unless you are re-fitting the draft planner.

options.name: tf_ds_decode_dec
options.label: Decode tensor-core kernels
options.doc: Decode rounds use tensor-core kernels for the dense and expert layers. Set it to 0 to fall back to the plain vector kernels, the reference path, which measured slower. Leave it on.

options.name: tf_ds_decode_fuse
options.label: Fuse decode expert sum
options.doc: Folds the sum of a decode layer's routed experts into the down-projection launch, one launch fewer per layer. The result is the same arithmetic in the same order. It also changes what the SSD cache considers the same computation, so switching it makes saved conversations recompute once. Every server process must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_decode_sab
options.label: Decode on the swap-A/B kernels
options.doc: Runs decode launches on the swapped-operand matrix multiply instead of the vector kernels. The vector kernels are faster at decode sizes, so leave it off.

options.name: tf_ds_dec_pdl
options.label: Overlap decode kernel launches
options.doc: Decode kernels start while the previous kernel is finishing (programmatic dependent launch). Set it to 0 to launch them one after another; the kernels and results are the same. Normally left on.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_4way
options.label: Drafter split four ways
options.doc: Splits the drafter's stages across all four nodes, like the main model, instead of two nodes holding the same halves. Frees about 2 GB per node and measured 3% faster for one stream and 4% at 16 streams. It needs the model's own weights and the four-node layout. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tensorfold_loop_windows
options.label: Loop guard: dry windows
options.doc: With the loop guard on, how many dry windows in a row close the think block (built-in 10). 0 closes it only when a cycle repeats exactly.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_main_4way
options.label: Drafter main projection split
options.doc: Each node loads and multiplies only its quarter of the drafter's main projection instead of all of it on every absorb. Same results, about 1% faster for one stream. Needs the four-node layout; every node must agree. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_ms
options.label: Draft pass cost
options.doc: How many milliseconds the planner assumes a drafter pass and absorb add to each round when deciding how many drafts to verify. The built-in 6.6 ms is measured on this four-node setup. Change it only when tuning the draft planner.

options.name: tf_seed_random
options.label: Random seed when none is sent
options.doc: Set to 1 so identical requests that send no seed sample differently: a value taken from the clock and a counter is mixed into the seed. Off, the seed follows the prompt alone, so the same request samples the same reply. A request's own seed is always kept exactly.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_woa
options.label: Drafter attention output precision
options.doc: Chooses the storage of the drafter's attention output weights: fp8 by default, or bf16 to match the main model's full-size rows. Affects drafter memory and speed only.

options.name: tf_ds_fix_k
options.label: Fixed drafts per round
options.doc: Diagnostics: forces every drafted stream to verify exactly this many draft tokens a round instead of letting the planner choose. Used for measurements; leave unset in normal use.

options.name: tf_ds_head_cand
options.label: Candidates from each node's head columns

options.name: tf_ds_head_pack12
options.label: Packed output head
options.doc: Selects the packed form of the main model's output head for decode rounds only; it changes nothing a prompt pass stores. A speed switch kept for comparison; every node must agree. Leave it as shipped.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_dec_mb
options.label: Decode prefetch for shared expert
options.doc: How much of the shared expert's weights, in MiB, a decode round prefetches into the GPU cache ahead of use (built-in 8). Affects speed only; change it only when tuning cache behaviour.

options.name: tf_ds_round_ms
options.default_text: Built-in table for the four-node lane
options.label: Round cost table
options.doc: A comma-separated list of how long a decode round takes for each number of rows (milliseconds). The draft planner uses it to decide how many drafts are worth verifying. The built-in table is measured for the four-node setup; change it only when re-tuning the planner.

options.name: tf_ds_served_k
options.label: Limit drafts to the planner's choice
options.doc: Caps how many drafts a stream verifies at the planner's own choice: all (every stream count), solo (a lone stream only), or off. Used when tuning how aggressively the engine drafts.

options.name: tf_head_geometry
options.label: Head kernel geometry (benchmark)
options.doc: Diagnostics: forces the output-head kernel's launch geometry in the Nemotron level benchmark. Not read in normal serving. Leave it unset.

options.name: tf_top_k_max
options.label: Largest top-k
options.doc: The largest top_k the sampler takes. A request's top_k of 0 or below then means the server's default, and one above this value is cut to it, with a warning at most once a minute. Unset or 0, requests' top_k values are used as sent.

options.name: cuda_device_max_connections
options.label: CUDA hardware queues
options.doc: NVIDIA's own setting for how many hardware work queues the GPU context gets (driver default 8). More queues let a prompt pass and decode rounds run side by side without waiting on one queue. The DeepSeek engine sets 16 at its own start when you leave it unset (the stagger's second pass needs it).

options.name: mcdma_rpcd_socket
options.label: MCDMA listener socket (library)
options.doc: Diagnostics: the socket path the fabric helper library uses to register with its listen daemon. Not used by the normal four-node deployment; leave unset.

options.name: mcdma_rpc_box_dir
options.label: MCDMA mailbox folder (tests)
options.doc: Diagnostics: a folder for the fabric helper library's mailbox files, used by tests. Not used in normal serving; leave unset.

options.name: mcdma_rpc_library
options.label: MCDMA helper library path
options.doc: Diagnostics: the file path of the fabric helper library, used instead of the installed copy. Not used by the normal deployment; leave unset.

options.name: tf_cuda_device
options.label: GPU device number
options.doc: Which GPU on the machine the engine uses (0 for the first). Each Spark has one GPU, so it stays 0 here.

options.name: tf_cuda_proc_address
options.label: Launch through driver entry points
options.doc: Diagnostics: set to 1 to make kernel and graph launches go through the driver's looked-up entry points. A profiling aid; leave off in normal use.

options.name: tf_ds_cuda_events
options.label: How the first node waits on GPU events
options.doc: Set to blocking and the first node's engine thread sleeps while it waits for GPU events instead of spinning on a fast CPU core. With 16 streams decoding that dropped that thread's CPU use from 91% to 4% and cooled the hottest core, with speed and replies unchanged. Any other value is ignored with a warning. The DeepSeek engine sets this to blocking at its own start when you leave it unset (measured: speed unchanged, the spinning threads gone); other engines keep the driver default.

options.name: tf_ds_cuda_sched
options.label: How host threads wait for the GPU
options.doc: How host threads wait for the GPU: auto, spin or yield keep a thread busy in some way, and blocking makes engine threads sleep in a synchronize call until the GPU is done instead of spinning on a CPU core. Measured 3 to 7 C cooler under decoding with speed and replies unchanged. Unset leaves the driver's default, which spins. The DeepSeek engine sets this to blocking at its own start when you leave it unset (measured: speed unchanged, the spinning threads gone); other engines keep the driver default.

options.name: tf_ds_kit
options.label: Kernel kit folder
options.doc: The folder holding the kernel kit that lives outside the container image: compiled GPU kernels, rotary-position tables and the Engram description. Set by the deployment; do not change it by hand.

options.name: tf_ds_kit_id
options.label: Kernel kit identity
options.doc: A label naming the kernel kit version. It is part of the SSD cache's identity, so a different kit never reuses saved conversations. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_collect_peers
options.label: Collect from every peer at once

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_cpus
options.label: CPU cores for RDMA proxies
options.doc: Three CPU core numbers, comma separated, that the decode rings' proxy threads run on (the four-node ring, the column pair and the row pair). Unset lets the system place them. On these machines the small cores 0, 10 and 11 were used.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_devices
options.label: RDMA devices for decode exchanges
options.doc: The network devices, one per rail, that carry the decode exchanges between nodes over RDMA. Set by the deployment for the two-rail setup; the engine refuses to start decoding on four nodes without them.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_gid
options.default_text: Each device's first RoCE v2 address
options.label: RDMA address index
options.doc: The GID index used on every RDMA device. Unset, each device's first RoCE v2 IPv4 address is used, which is what this cluster needs.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_kernels
options.label: RDMA kernel file
options.doc: The compiled GPU kernel file for the RDMA gathers. Unset uses the one built into the engine; set only to test a different build.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_nap_us
options.label: Longest RDMA proxy nap
options.doc: With proxy napping on, the longest a nap lasts in microseconds (built-in 50, capped at 2,500). A nap ends early when the doorbell is rung, so this only bounds the delay if a doorbell is missed.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_pdl
options.label: Overlap RDMA kernel launches
options.doc: RDMA ring kernels start while the previous kernel is finishing. Set to 0 to launch them one after another; the results are the same. Normally left on.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_prefix
options.label: RDMA subnet prefix length
options.doc: How many address bits two RDMA devices must share to count as being on the same subnet and so as a pair (built-in 24). Change only if the fabric addressing changes.

options.name: tf_ds_rdma_wfe
options.label: RDMA proxies nap instead of polling

options.name: tf_ds_ring_dead_ms
options.label: Ring progress timeout
options.doc: How long, in milliseconds, a decode ring may make no progress before the engine fails it by name instead of hanging. Whole number from 1; unset uses the built-in limit.

options.name: tf_ds_ring_inplace
options.label: Write straight into send slots
options.doc: Producers of decode exchanges write their part directly into the send slot and publish it, so the staging copy is gone. Needs write-combined slots; with more than two streams on one ring the start is refused. Every node must agree. On by default: it is a bit-identical speed change (replies equal byte for byte on the four Sparks), so an engine started with nothing set runs it. With no RDMA ring, or without the write-combined slots, the start line says it is off and the engine goes on without it. Set it to 0 to turn it off (a run that gathers on more than two CUDA streams on one ring needs that).

options.name: tf_ds_ring_wc
options.label: Write-combined ring slots
options.doc: The rings' send and landing slots live in write-combined host memory registered with the network card, which lets the GPU write them directly. A prerequisite for writing straight into send slots. Every node must agree. On by default: it is a bit-identical speed change (replies equal byte for byte on the four Sparks), so an engine started with nothing set runs it. With no RDMA ring the start line says it is off and the engine goes on without it. Set it to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_ring_word
options.label: Generation word signalling
options.doc: On by default: each ring lane's data goes as a plain RDMA write and a 64-bit generation word is written after it to say it has arrived; the collecting kernel waits on those words. Set 0 for the flag-based arrival (the proxy publishes each lane's flag). The card's wait for the decode rings needs this on, with either arrival signal. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_ring_word_deadline_ms
options.label: Generation word wait limit
options.doc: How long a lane waits for its generation word, in milliseconds (built-in 120,000), before the ring is failed. 0 or an unreadable value uses the built-in.

options.name: tf_ds_ring_word_signal
options.label: Generation word signal type
options.doc: How the generation word is sent: by default an RDMA atomic add, which the card executes only after the data writes are placed (the guaranteed arrival); word sends an 8-byte RDMA write instead. Every node must agree. A card without atomics: left unset, the rings send the write and say why in a warning; set to atomic, the start refuses by name.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_combine_door
options.label: Rocinante: sum and signal in one launch
options.doc: In Rocinante, the engine's own transport for prompt passes, the mixture-of-experts routed sum runs in one launch that also rings the send doorbell. A speed option; every node must agree. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_cpus
options.label: Rocinante proxy cores
options.doc: The CPU cores for Rocinante's proxy threads on its first lane. Unset leaves them to the system. Pinning them to the small cores was measured to change nothing in speed.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_cpus_b
options.label: Rocinante proxy cores, second lane
options.doc: The two CPU cores for Rocinante's second lane's proxies (built-in 1,2, small cores that neither the decode rings' proxies nor the first lane use).

options.name: tf_ds_roci_cpus_h
options.label: Rocinante proxy cores, host lane
options.doc: The two CPU cores for the host lane's proxies. Unset they are not pinned and sleep in the kernel between looks. A core already used by another proxy is refused.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_engram_ahead
options.label: Rocinante: Engram a layer ahead
options.doc: Rocinante sends an Engram layer's first part right after its projection, so the projection is done a layer ahead of use. A speed option for prompt passes; every node must agree. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_p2_first
options.label: Rocinante: send second part first
options.doc: The add that makes an owner sum's second part runs first and the send follows at once, ahead of other work. A speed option for prompt passes; every node must agree. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_pair_log
options.label: Pass-pair timing log
options.doc: Diagnostics: prints extra log lines about the two passes in flight and the Engram reader's thread. Leave unset in normal use.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_sent_first
options.label: Rocinante: sum in the sending launch
options.doc: One launch does the routed sum in this order and rings the doorbell from inside, instead of four launches. A speed option for prompt passes; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_stagger
options.label: Two prompt passes in flight
options.doc: Runs two consecutive whole prompt passes at once, one on each of a node's two Rocinante lanes, with the second pass's layers running just behind the first's. Needs every exchange of a pass on Rocinante. Replies unchanged. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_stagger_gap
options.label: Stagger lag between passes
options.doc: How many layers the second pass lags the first when two passes are in flight: 1, 2 or 3. Results do not depend on it, only speed.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_stagger_prio
options.label: Stagger stream priority
options.doc: Stream priority of the two staggered passes: 0 equal (default), 1 the first pass above the second, 2 the second above the first (a control). Only matters with two passes in flight.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_worker_pair_major
options.label: Engram order for paired passes
options.doc: With two passes in flight, the Engram reader reads both passes' layer 0 first, then both passes' layer 1, and so on, in groups of 4 chunks. Only matters with two passes in flight.

options.name: tf_fabric_verbs
options.label: Fabric verbs test switch
options.doc: Diagnostics: turns on a fabric library test that needs real RDMA hardware. Not read in serving; leave unset.

options.name: tf_rdma_devices
options.label: RDMA devices (Python-lane name)
options.doc: The network devices that carry the decode exchanges over RDMA, under the name the earlier Python build used. An empty value counts as unset. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_rdma_pdl
options.label: Overlap RDMA kernels (Python-lane name)
options.doc: The earlier Python build's name for the overlap-RDMA-kernel-launches option: 0 launches them one after another. Normally left unset.

options.name: tf_tp_listen
options.default_text: The master address for every node
options.label: Rank 0 listen addresses
options.doc: On the first node, the address it listens on for each of the three other nodes, comma separated. Unset, each uses the master address. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_tp_local
options.label: Single-process test mode
options.doc: Diagnostics: serves every job at once on the spot and sends nothing, to time the GPU side alone. Replies are wrong in this mode; never use it for serving.

options.name: tf_tp_master
options.label: Rank 0 address
options.doc: The first node's address on the fabric, which the other nodes connect to when the engine starts. Set by the deployment; it must be an IP address.

options.name: tf_tp_port
options.label: Rank 0 port
options.doc: The port on the first node the other nodes connect to (built-in 29620). Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_tp_stats
options.label: Job timing statistics
options.doc: Diagnostics: prints the host's time from a job's post to its serve every 4,096 jobs. Leave unset in normal use.

options.name: tf_tp_trace
options.label: Job trace
options.doc: Diagnostics: logs every job the host serves, which is very verbose. Leave unset in normal use.

options.name: tf_tp_world
options.label: Number of nodes
options.doc: How many nodes work together (the native engine supports two GPUs or the four-node split; the unset default is 2). Set to 4 for this cluster by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_engram
options.label: Engram tables folder
options.doc: The folder holding the model's Engram tables, which each node reads from its own disk. Set by the deployment; changing it points the engine at different tables.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_ahead_pass
options.label: Engram rows read pass by pass

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio
options.label: Engram reads by asynchronous disk I/O

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_depth
options.label: Engram reads in flight (prompts)
options.doc: The most Engram disk reads a prompt's I/O ring keeps in flight at once (built-in 256, 0 for no cap). An over-queued drive loses throughput and the submit call blocks, so a cap smooths prompt processing.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_sleep
options.label: Engram waiters sleep for disk
options.doc: On unless set to 0. A prompt's Engram disk waiters sleep in the kernel until a batch of reads completes instead of polling, which frees a CPU core. Decode rounds' ring keeps polling.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_slice
options.label: Engram reads submitted at a time
options.doc: How many Engram reads are submitted to the disk at once as earlier ones complete (built-in 64). Smaller slices avoid over-queueing the drive.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_spin
options.label: Empty polls before sleeping
options.doc: How many polls that find no finished Engram read a waiter makes before it goes to sleep (built-in 2). Only applies when the sleeping waiters option is on.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_wake
options.label: Completions that wake a sleeper
options.doc: How many finished Engram reads a sleeping waiter waits for before waking (built-in 32). Larger numbers wake less often.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_aio_wake_us
options.label: Longest Engram sleep
options.doc: The longest, in microseconds, a sleeping Engram waiter sleeps before checking anyway (built-in 1,000).

options.name: tf_ds_engram_cache_mib
options.label: Engram row cache size
options.doc: How much memory, in MiB, the Engram row cache gets across both Engram layers (built-in 2,048; 0 turns the cache off). It keeps recently read rows so fewer reads hit the disk. Needs the packed Engram shards.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_fault
options.label: Engram failure drill
options.doc: Diagnostics: makes one named node's Engram reader fail one read, written as node:count, to test how the engine copes with a disk error. Leave unset in normal use.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_instream
options.label: Engram landing as a stream step
options.doc: Each decode round's Engram rows are landed as a step on the GPU stream instead of a separate host copy. A speed option for decode; it also changes what the SSD cache considers the same computation.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_keep_ahead
options.label: Keep Engram reader across decode rounds
options.doc: While a long prompt is processed, the decode round that runs between its chunks leaves the Engram reader and the rows it read ahead in place instead of discarding them. Needs asynchronous Engram reads; it only has effect with decode rounds between chunks. On by default: measured +0.5 to +1.5 % beside generating requests, replies equal. Where it cannot run (the Engram reads are not asynchronous: TF_DS_ENGRAM_AIO=0) the engine turns it off with one warning naming why; set to 1 yourself and that refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_wait_us
options.label: Engram wait before looking again
options.doc: How long, in microseconds, the engine thread sleeps for the Engram reader's rows before it checks again for events no wake-up announces. The waits sleep rather than spin, so this only bounds the worst-case delay.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_packed
options.default_text: Not set (rows read from the tables)
options.label: Packed Engram shards folder
options.doc: Reads Engram rows from the folder of shards made by the Engram packing tool: one record per row, kept in a row cache and decoded on the GPU, so each row is one read. Several Engram options need it.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_partner
options.label: Share Engram reads between partners
options.doc: Two nodes that need the same Engram rows read half each and swap them over a spare RDMA lane instead of both reading everything from disk. Every node must agree. On by default: it halves every node's Engram disk reads at equal speed, replies equal. It needs whole Engram tables on every node, packed shards and the four-node 2D split with Rocinante; where one of those fails on any node the engine turns it off with one warning naming why; set to 1 yourself and that refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_partner_split
options.label: Engram partner split (test)
options.doc: Diagnostics: set to 0 to open the partner lane but send nothing across it, to tell what the open lane costs from what the split costs. Leave on in normal use.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_revision
options.label: Engram revision label
options.doc: A label that is part of the SSD cache's identity. Changing it makes cached conversations from before count as made by different tables, so they recompute once.

options.name: tf_ds_engram_worker
options.label: Engram reader thread
options.doc: A background thread reads a prompt's Engram rows ahead of the GPU. Set to 0 to turn it off; Engram rows are then read by the engine thread as it needs them, which is slower. Leave on.

options.name: tf_ds_image_cache
options.label: Cache images with their conversation
options.doc: Keeps images seen in a conversation so its saved state can resume with them, in memory and on the SSD. Set to 0 and images are not kept: a conversation with images recomputes. On by default.

options.name: tf_ds_rank_cache
options.label: Per-node weight files folder
options.doc: The folder holding each node's own weight file, read from its own disk. Set by the deployment and checked against the image before start; do not change it by hand.

options.name: tf_ds_rank_cache_sha
options.label: Weight file fingerprint
options.doc: The SHA-256 fingerprint of a node's weight file. The SSD cache includes it in a saved state's identity, so a different set of weights never reuses another's cache. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_backlog_gib
options.label: SSD write backlog limit
options.doc: How much unwritten data, in GiB, may queue for the SSD before the engine refuses to keep another conversation (built-in 16). A refused keep means that conversation recomputes later instead of loading from disk.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_dir
options.default_text: Required when the SSD cache is on
options.label: SSD cache folder
options.doc: The folder on the first node where kept conversation states are stored on its NVMe. Must be an absolute path.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_gib
options.label: SSD cache size
options.doc: How much the SSD cache may hold, in GiB (0 is off, the default). With a cap, conversation states that leave memory are kept on disk, so a conversation can resume after memory evicts it or after a restart of the same build instead of recomputing.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_ioprio
options.label: SSD cache I/O priority
options.doc: The disk priority of the SSD cache's threads: best-effort 0 to 7 (built-in be/7, the lowest of those), idle, or none to leave it as is. A lower priority keeps cache traffic from slowing other disk use.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_keep_builds
options.label: Older builds' SSD stores kept
options.doc: How many earlier builds' SSD cache stores to keep beside the current one's (built-in 1; 0 to 16). Stores from other builds cannot be reused but occupy disk until pruned.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_land_piece_mib
options.label: SSD restore piece size
options.doc: The size, in MiB, of each piece when a restored conversation state is broadcast to all nodes (built-in 32). Affects restore speed and buffer use.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_land_slots
options.label: SSD restore landing buffers
options.doc: How many landing buffers every node preallocates for restores from the SSD (built-in 2). If none is free, the restore is skipped and the request runs from memory or recomputes.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_min_free_gib
options.label: SSD free-space floor
options.doc: No SSD cache write may leave less than this much free on the disk, in GiB (built-in 50). Protects the disk from being filled by the cache.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_min_tokens
options.label: Shortest state kept on SSD
options.doc: Conversation states shorter than this many tokens are not written to the SSD cache (built-in 8,192), since recomputing them is cheap.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_off_reason
options.label: SSD cache off reason
options.doc: Set text here to switch the SSD cache off and have the status say why. Used by the deployment tools; leave unset normally.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_open_ms
options.label: SSD cache open timeout
options.doc: How long the start waits for the SSD cache store to open before serving without it (built-in 300,000 ms, five minutes). Past it the cache is off until the next start.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_probe_every
options.label: SSD cache consistency re-check
options.doc: The SSD cache stores one copy for all nodes, so it checks at start that every node holds identical bytes. This repeats a sampled check every this many kept conversations (0 means start only).

options.name: tf_ds_spill_probe_rows
options.label: SSD consistency check rows
options.doc: How many extra rows each plane a consistency check samples, besides the first and last (built-in 8, up to 62). More rows check more but take longer.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_probe_tokens
options.label: SSD consistency probe length
options.doc: The length, in tokens, of the prompt the start-up consistency check runs (built-in 8,192).

options.name: tf_ds_spill_quota
options.label: One conversation's share of SSD
options.doc: The largest fraction of the SSD cache a single conversation may use, from 0 to 1 (0 means no limit). Stops one long conversation crowding out the others.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_readers
options.label: SSD reader threads
options.doc: How many threads read from the SSD cache (built-in 4, 1 to 64). More allows faster restores if the disk keeps up.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_restores
options.label: Simultaneous SSD restores
options.doc: How many conversation restores from the SSD may run at once (built-in 2, 1 to 16). Each needs a small staging slot.

options.name: tf_ds_spill_smalls
options.label: SSD small-state slots
options.doc: How many slots hold small conversation states waiting to be written to the SSD (built-in 4, 1 to 64).

options.name: tf_ds_spill_staging_mib
options.label: SSD staging memory
options.doc: Pinned host memory, in MiB, used to stage SSD cache writes, reads and small states together (built-in 128).

options.name: tf_ds_token_map
options.label: Compressed token map
options.doc: The file for the Engram compressed token map. Set by the deployment; it is part of the SSD cache identity, so changing it makes cached conversations recompute.

options.name: tf_spill_defer_min
options.label: Shortest restore worth waiting for
options.doc: The shortest restore, in tokens, worth deferring a request for when the SSD has no room. 0 uses the model's own step size.

options.name: tf_spill_defer_ms
options.label: Wait for a refused SSD restore
options.doc: How long a request whose SSD restore was refused for lack of room waits without any restore finishing, before it runs on what memory holds (built-in 5,000 ms; 0 means at once).

options.name: tf_spill_defer_retry_ms
options.label: Deferred restore retry interval
options.doc: How soon a deferred request asks the SSD cache again (built-in 25 ms).

options.name: tf_spill_flush_ms
options.label: SSD flush time at shutdown
options.doc: The longest a clean stop waits for pending SSD writes to finish (built-in 15,000 ms).

options.name: tf_spill_load_ms
options.label: SSD work per service round
options.doc: The time budget for all SSD restores in one service round, after which staged writes get time (built-in 40 ms). Bounds how much a restore can delay decoding.

options.name: tf_spill_load_wait_ms
options.label: Longest wait for an SSD restore
options.doc: The longest a request waits in all for its SSD restore (built-in 30,000 ms) before it is admitted without it and recomputes.

options.name: tf_spill_poll_ms
options.label: SSD idle poll interval
options.doc: How often the idle host checks restores, staged writes and deferred retries (built-in 2 ms).

options.name: tf_spill_pump_ms
options.label: SSD write share while decoding
options.doc: The slice of each service round given to staging SSD writes while streams are decoding (built-in 2 ms; never more than the per-round budget).

options.name: tf_spill_test_dir
options.label: SSD tests' scratch folder
options.doc: Diagnostics: where the SSD cache's own tests put their scratch files. Not read in serving.

options.name: tf_spill_turns
options.label: Old turns kept first
options.doc: How many old turns of a conversation's active path are kept before they are the first to go when the SSD is full (built-in 4; 0 keeps until room is needed).

options.name: tensorfold_cuda_memory_limit_gb
options.label: GPU memory ceiling
options.doc: An upper bound on the memory the engine may allocate on the GPU, in GiB. Unset means only the free-memory reserve limits it. A start with an invalid number is refused.

options.name: tensorfold_memory_reserve_gib
options.default_text: A tenth of the memory, at least 4 GiB
options.label: Memory kept free
options.doc: How much memory, in GiB, the engine leaves free when it admits allocations (at least 2). The default is a tenth of the memory and at least 4 GiB. Raise it if the machine itself runs short; lower it to give the engine more.

options.name: tf_ds_arena_gib
options.label: Initial GPU buffer block
options.doc: Reserves a first block of device memory, in GiB, for the engine's buffers at start. Unset lets the buffers take what they need. Normally left to the memory sizing options.

options.name: tf_ds_direct_weights
options.label: Direct weight reads
options.doc: Reads each node's weight file straight from its disk, past the page cache, so every byte is read once and the cache is not filled. Set it to 0 to read through the page cache as before. Leave it on.

options.name: tf_ds_window
options.label: KV pool size
options.doc: The number of token positions all streams share in the KV pool. Unset, the pool is exactly the context; it can never be smaller than the context, so one full request always fits (the context is never lowered). A larger pool keeps more conversations whole beside live streams but takes memory on every node. Cannot be combined with the free-memory target.

options.default_text: Off (pool sized by the pool-size setting)
options.name: tf_ds_kv_free_target_gib
options.label: KV pool by free-memory target
options.doc: Sizes the KV pool automatically: the pool is the most positions that fit on all four nodes while each keeps this many GiB free. It is never smaller than the context. A start that cannot fit the context with this much free is refused and names the shortfall. Cannot be combined with the pool size setting; every node must use the same value. With TF_DS_KV_VMM=1 a change while the engine runs resizes the pool live on every Spark: it grows or gives back its tail so each Spark keeps this much free (the ranks take the smallest fit, never below the context, never under an extent a stream or a kept conversation holds: a shrink stops there and says so); without TF_DS_KV_VMM it applies at the next start.

options.default_text: Measured per node role (9.25 GiB first node, 7.5 GiB others)
options.name: tf_ds_kv_growth_mib
options.label: Memory left after the KV pool
options.doc: With the free-memory target, how much memory (MiB) to leave for what the engine allocates after the pool is placed and while it serves. Unset uses measured allowances: 9.25 GiB on the first node and 7.5 GiB on the others. A number given here applies to every node.

options.name: home
options.label: Home folder
options.doc: The home folder of the engine's user. Learned prompt states and the model download cache default to folders under it unless told otherwise. Set by the system; do not change.

options.name: tensorfold_cuda_kernels
options.default_text: The kernel set beside the engine
options.label: GPU kernel folder
options.doc: The folder of precompiled GPU kernels for this GPU model. Unset, the engine looks in its own install folder for the kernel set matching the GPU. The start is refused if none is found.

options.name: tf_cluster_probes
options.label: Cluster test: probe files
options.doc: Diagnostics: a folder of recorded probe output used only by an opt-in cluster-topology test. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_cluster_report
options.label: Cluster test: report switch
options.doc: Diagnostics: used only by an opt-in cluster test that prints its report when this is set. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_coop_split
options.label: Nemotron: split column tiles
options.doc: For the Nemotron model family only: set to 0 to keep one thread group per column tile, as the earlier Python engine did, instead of splitting. Not used by the DeepSeek engine.

options.name: tf_cuda_segments
options.label: CUDA segments
options.doc: How many segments (1 to 4, built-in 1) the single-machine CUDA engine splits its work into; the command line flag overrides it. Not used by the four-node deployment.

options.name: tensorfold_stats_every
options.label: Stats line interval
options.doc: As requests finish, a stats line at most this often, in seconds, about what finished since the last one: tokens a round, drafts kept, and the draft head's chains by depth. 0, the default, writes none. Replies are the same either way.

options.name: tf_ds_2d_gu
options.label: Experts' gate/up split mode
options.doc: Set to parity to give each node pair half of every expert's gate and up blocks, with the odd ninth block shared by parity, for a balanced split of the experts. Changes how weights are laid out; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_2d_order
options.label: Node order in the 2D split
options.doc: The order the four nodes take in the 2D split, as four numbers such as 0,1,2,3 (a test used 0,2,1,3). Unset, nodes follow their rank. Set by the deployment; a wrong order mixes up the nodes.

options.name: tf_ds_ablation_id
options.label: Weights ablation identity
options.doc: A label naming the weights' ablation variant and its revision (or none). It is part of the SSD cache's identity so saved conversations are never reused under different weights. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_assemble_quant
options.label: Assemble and quantize in one launch
options.doc: In the four-node split, assembles a chunk's expert intermediate and computes the down projection's quantization of it in one launch instead of two. A speed option for prompts; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_attn_epilogue
options.label: Attention epilogue in one launch
options.doc: A prompt chunk's attention output gets its inverse rotary embedding and the quantization for the next projection in one launch instead of separate ones. A speed option for prompts; every node must agree. On by default: it is a bit-identical speed change (replies equal byte for byte on the four Sparks), so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where its condition fails (not the checkpoint's own weights) the start line says it is off and the engine goes on without it. Set it to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tensorfold_reply_ids
options.label: Reply markers by token
options.doc: Set to 1 to read where a reply's think block and tool calls open and close by their marker tokens instead of by the reply's text, and to keep marker-like text in an assistant turn as words when it is sent back. It came with the base engine and has not been tested with this model.

options.name: tf_ds_connect_s
options.label: Follower connect retry time
options.doc: How long, in seconds, a follower node keeps retrying its connection to the first node at start (built-in 300). Raise it if nodes start far apart in time.

options.name: tf_ds_engine_id
options.label: Engine image identity
options.doc: A label naming the engine image and its configuration. It is part of the SSD cache's identity and must be the same on every node. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_gemm_halves
options.label: Split passes over 4,096 rows
options.doc: A prompt pass of more than 4,096 rows runs its dense matrix multiplies as row blocks of at most 4,096, each the same launch a 4,096-row pass makes. It has no effect on passes of 2,048 rows, such as beside decoding. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_gemm_r2
options.label: Exact expert GEMM: padding-free kernels
options.doc: With the exact-arithmetic matrix multiplies, uses kernels that leave out padding rows' copies and give the down projection a 128-row tile. Replies are unchanged. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_gemm_w16
options.label: Exact GEMM on 16 warps
options.doc: A prompt chunk's exact-arithmetic matrix multiplies and the attention output rows run on 16 warps per block instead of fewer. A speed option; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_hc_fused
options.label: Fuse mix and finish for prompts
options.doc: A prompt chunk's hyper-connection mixes and their finish run in one launch from the kernel kit's extra set, with the same block partials in the same order. A speed option; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_hc_late_fork
options.label: Launch mix side work later
options.doc: In decode, the mixes' side work (stored-stream dots and Sinkhorn) is launched after the main stream's next kernel instead of before it, so the main work is not held up. Same kernels and bytes. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_hc_side
options.label: Mix side work on its own stream
options.doc: Runs the hyper-connection mixes' side work on a stream of its own so it overlaps the main work. Needs the model's own weights; on only when set to anything but 0.

options.name: tf_ds_hc_stride
options.label: Read gathered planes in place
options.doc: In the four-node split, a quarter-HC layer's mixes read the gathered planes where they lie at the chunk's own stride instead of from a tight repack. Same bits. Every node must agree. On by default: it is a bit-identical speed change (replies equal byte for byte on the four Sparks), so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where its condition fails (needs the four-node 2D split with quarter hidden-state mixes) the start line says it is off and the engine goes on without it. Set it to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_ds_idx_v
options.label: Indexer scores, key tile once
options.doc: A prompt chunk's indexer scores come from a kernel variant that dequantizes the key tile once per program and reuses it for its rows. A speed option for prompts; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_issue_lead_slice_us
options.label: Issue lead wait slice
options.doc: When the issue lead makes the host wait, how long in microseconds each wait slice lasts (built-in 100, 1 to 100,000).

options.name: tf_ds_issue_lead_wait
options.label: Issue lead wait method
options.doc: How the host waits when the issue lead holds it back: poll (the default, keeps checking) or block (sleeps until the GPU gets there).

options.name: tf_ds_issue_lead_warn_ms
options.label: Issue lead warning delay
options.doc: How long, in milliseconds, the host may wait on the issue lead before it logs a warning line saying where it is (built-in 2,000; 0 never warns). Never fatal.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_attn_mb
options.label: L2 prefetch: attention
options.doc: How much of the attention weights, in MiB, the paced prefetch pulls into the GPU's L2 cache after the query is computed (built-in 16). Affects decode speed only; needs the L2 prefetch option on.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_dn_mb
options.label: L2 prefetch: expert down weights
options.doc: How much of the active experts' down-projection weights, in MiB, is prefetched into L2 beside the network exchange (built-in 8; 0 none).

options.name: tf_ds_l2_moe_mb
options.label: L2 prefetch: experts
options.doc: How much of the mixture-of-experts weights, in MiB, the paced prefetch pulls into L2 ahead of use (built-in 8).

options.name: tf_ds_l2_next_mb
options.label: L2 prefetch: next layer
options.doc: How much of the next layer's weights, in MiB, the paced prefetch pulls into L2 (built-in 16).

options.name: tf_ds_l2_prefetch
options.label: Paced L2 prefetch
options.doc: Prefetches the next kernels' weights into the GPU's L2 cache at a paced rate while earlier kernels run, hiding memory latency in decoding. Off unless set to anything but 0.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_skip
options.label: L2 prefetch skip mask (measurement)
options.doc: Diagnostics: a bit mask of L2 prefetches to leave out (1 attention fork, 2 experts fork, and so on), to measure what each contributes. Leave unset.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_stretch_end_mb
options.label: L2 prefetch: end of stretch
options.doc: How much weight data, in MiB, is prefetched into L2 at the end of a stretch of layers (built-in 4).

options.name: tf_ds_mma_sf
options.label: Prompt GEMMs on block-scaled MMA
options.doc: A prompt chunk's FP8 matrix multiplies (dense and the experts' gate/up and down) run on the tensor core's block-scaled instruction, which accumulates each split in the tensor core. Faster, but the arithmetic differs; see the exact variant for identical bits. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_model_revision
options.label: Model revision label
options.doc: A label naming the model checkpoint revision. It is part of the SSD cache's identity so saved conversations are never reused with a different checkpoint. Set by the deployment.

options.name: tf_ds_no_copies
options.label: No copied continuations
options.doc: Decode windows never take a copied continuation of the stream's own text, only the drafter's drafts. Replies are the same either way; copies just make some edits faster, so turning them off only slows those.

options.name: tf_ds_par_one
options.label: Parity gate/up in one launch
options.doc: In the parity expert split, decode runs gate and up in a single launch with the same bits. On by default; set to 0 for the older two-launch way.

options.name: tf_ds_pdl
options.label: Overlap kernel launches
options.doc: Launches use the programmatic-dependent-launch attribute so each kernel starts while the one before finishes. Set to 0 to launch everything the ordinary way; this is the master switch for the other overlap options. Normally left on.

options.name: tf_ds_triton_pdl_attr
options.label: Overlap captured kernel launches
options.doc: Kernels recorded into decode graphs carry the overlap attribute so they start early. Set to 0 to launch them the ordinary way; the kernels are unchanged. Normally left on.

options.name: tf_ds_woa_w8
options.label: Attention output from FP8 rows
options.doc: Loads the attention output weights from their FP8 rows only and leaves out the bf16 copy, saving about 0.67 GB per node (16.8 MB a layer). A prompt chunk converts them as needed; speed measured unchanged. Every node must agree. On by default: it is a measured win, so an engine started with nothing set runs it. Where a condition it needs fails (named in the start line), it turns itself off with one warning naming why and what it costs; set to 1 yourself and a failed condition refuses the start by name; set to 0 to turn it off.

options.name: tf_exl3_l2_delay_ns
options.label: L2 prefetch pacing delay
options.doc: The delay in nanoseconds between the paced L2 prefetch's chunks (used with the prefetch rate). A tuning knob for the L2 prefetch; leave at default.

options.name: tf_exl3_l2_rate_gbps
options.label: L2 prefetch rate
options.doc: The rate in GB/s at which the paced L2 prefetch pulls weights (0 means every chunk at once). A tuning knob for the L2 prefetch; leave at default.

options.name: tf_flashnext_tp
options.label: Flash Next two-Mac mode
options.doc: For the Mac-based Flash Next engine only: names the settings for running as two cooperating Macs in lockstep. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: tf_k3_dir
options.label: Cluster test: model folder
options.doc: Diagnostics: a model folder used only by opt-in cluster estimation tests. Not read when serving.

options.name: tf_engine_cfg
options.label: Engine settings file
options.doc: The path of the engine's settings file, with one 'name = value' line per option (by id, name or environment name). A value in the file replaces the environment's, except for debug options, and options left out keep the environment's. A change made while the engine is stopped is recorded in a history file beside it at the next start.

options.name: tensorfold_admin_key_file
options.label: Admin key file
options.doc: The file holding the admin API's own keys, one 'label: key' line each, with file mode 0600 and keys of at least 32 bytes that differ from the normal API keys. Unset, every admin address answers as if it did not exist.

options.name: fz_call_log
options.label: Flash Next: prompt call log
options.doc: Diagnostics for the Mac-based Flash Next engine: logs one line after a prompt's first token with each call's rows, parts, and wall and GPU time. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: fz_gdn
options.label: Flash Next: GDN kernel variant
options.doc: For the Mac-based Flash Next engine only: chooses a variant of its gated delta-net kernels. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: fz_lane
options.label: Flash Next: lane kernels
options.doc: For the Mac-based Flash Next engine only: switches its lane and GDN kernels on for the target model, matching the recorded results. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: fz_pair_min
options.label: Flash Next: smallest pair chunk
options.doc: For the Mac-based Flash Next engine's two-Mac mode: the fewest rows each Mac takes of a paired chunk. The second Mac takes the first's value. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: glm_chunk
options.label: GLM: prompt chunk rows
options.doc: For the GLM model engine: the most rows in a prompt chunk. A smaller value is used to check that results do not depend on chunk size.

options.name: glm_copy
options.label: GLM: copy drafts
options.doc: For the GLM engine: a round copies what followed the reply's last N tokens earlier in the text (0 to 8; 0 is off), as draft tokens. Speed only.

options.name: glm_cuts
options.label: GLM: extra chunk cut
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM engine: a prompt chunk also ends at this position, to compare server and command-line runs.

options.name: glm_draft_vocab
options.label: GLM: drafter vocabulary size
options.doc: For the GLM engine: the multi-token-prediction head drafts only from the first this many tokens of the vocabulary (built-in 154,880).

options.name: glm_dry
options.label: GLM: dry run
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM engine: stops with a dry-run error after setup, before serving.

options.name: glm_ep
options.label: GLM: two-Mac expert split
options.doc: For the GLM engine on Macs: names this Mac's link settings to run half the experts here and half on a peer. Not used on the four-Spark cluster.

options.name: glm_ep_delay_us
options.label: GLM: slow link test delay
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM two-Mac mode: holds every prompt-chunk send over 1 MiB for this many microseconds, to simulate a slow link in stress tests.

options.name: glm_ep_split
options.label: GLM: expert split mode
options.doc: For the GLM two-Mac mode: the split is by rows by default; set to experts to split by experts instead.

options.name: glm_ep_trace
options.label: GLM: log every exchange
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM two-Mac mode: logs every exchange the host sends, which is very verbose.

options.name: glm_layers
options.label: GLM: layers to run
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM engine: loads and runs only the first N layers (the model has 45), for checks that must fit in memory.

options.name: glm_no_warmup
options.label: GLM: skip warm-up
options.doc: For the GLM engine: skips the one-time warm-up of a process's first prompt, which both Macs of a pair otherwise pay at the same step.

options.name: glm_prompt
options.label: GLM: chunked prompts
options.doc: For the GLM engine: prompts are processed in chunks unless set to 0.

options.name: glm_ranks
options.label: GLM: draft miss log
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM engine: keeps each drafting depth's logits and records where the target token ranked when a draft misses.

options.name: glm_residency
options.label: GLM: pin weights in memory
options.doc: For the GLM engine on a Mac: opt-in to pin about 181 GB of weights in memory, which leaves macOS nothing to reclaim if another model shares the Mac.

options.name: glm_route
options.label: GLM: fused router
options.doc: For the GLM engine: expert routing runs as fused launches unless set to 0, which uses the older separate cast, router and top-k launches.

options.name: glm_sparse_nax
options.label: GLM: sparse attention on tensor units
options.doc: For the GLM engine: the sparse attention runs on the tensor units unless set to 0, which uses the row-by-row kernel.

options.name: glm_tp
options.label: GLM: split heads across two Macs
options.doc: For the GLM engine: in a two-Mac pair, each Mac takes half the attention heads unless set to 0.

options.name: glm_windows
options.label: GLM: window timing log
options.doc: Diagnostics for the GLM engine: logs each window's streams, rows, GPU time and the idle gap before it.

options.name: tf_ds_clock_marks
options.label: GPU clock at every phase (profiling)
options.doc: Diagnostics: with profiling on, reads a GPU clock at every decode-round phase mark, including inside graphs. This splits the overlap chains, so stretch totals run longer than normal. Leave unset.

options.name: tf_ds_clock_ratio
options.label: Clock-timed compression ratio
options.doc: Diagnostics: which compression ratio's layers the third timing mode times (built-in 2). Used only when profiling.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_dump
options.label: Dump drafter tensors
options.doc: Diagnostics: a folder where the first node writes the drafter's inputs and one pass's intermediates for debugging. Off in service because it writes a lot of data.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_dump_pass
options.label: Drafter dump pass number
options.doc: Diagnostics: which drafter pass the tensor dump stops at (built-in 2). Only used with the drafter dump folder.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_log
options.label: Drafter draft log file
options.doc: Diagnostics: a file where the first node appends each drafter pass's drafts and confidences. A measurement aid, off in service.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_prof
options.label: Drafter pass profiling
options.doc: Diagnostics: runs drafter passes one step at a time with a synchronize at each mark to time them, which slows decoding. Off in service.

options.name: tf_ds_dump
options.label: Dump layer tensors
options.doc: Diagnostics: a folder where prompt tensors of chosen layers are written for debugging. Off in service because it writes a lot and slows prompts.

options.name: tf_ds_dump_layer
options.label: Layers to dump
options.doc: Diagnostics: a comma-separated list of layers for the tensor dump (built-in just layer 0), such as 0,8,19. Only used with the dump folder.

options.name: tf_ds_graph_fail_test
options.label: Graph capture failure drill
options.doc: Diagnostics: a test that makes one node's Nth graph capture report failure, written node:N, to check the fallback to plain launches. Never set in service.

options.name: tf_ds_prompt_trace
options.label: Prompt step trace
options.doc: Diagnostics: writes one log line for every prompt step the host serves or holds back, with the order policy's view of each admitted prompt, so a prompt that waited can be explained from the log.

options.name: tf_ds_replay_floor
options.label: Small chunk reads window from floor
options.doc: A small prompt chunk (16 rows or fewer) at a replay cut reads its window from the replay floor instead of the ring, which at the cut can still hold the previous request's keys. Without it a reply can depend on the request that came before. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_replay_only
options.label: Kernel replay: run only these sections
options.doc: Diagnostics: runs only the named sections of the kernel replay test, comma separated. Used by test tools; not read when serving.

options.name: tf_ds_ssd_fault
options.label: SSD failure drill
options.doc: Diagnostics: a test that makes one named node fail a write or corrupt an entry in its SSD store, to check the nodes' agreement gate, written write:rank or corrupt:rank. Never set in service.

options.name: tf_flashnext_dump
options.label: Flash Next: kernel dump folder
options.doc: For the Mac-based Flash Next engine: the folder of compiled kernels to use instead of the checked-in ones. Not used by this cluster.

options.name: tf_overlap_hot
options.label: Overlap tool: active experts
options.doc: Diagnostics for the overlap measuring tool: how many experts (6 to 384, built-in 384) a row's six routed picks are drawn from, to imitate routing that concentrates on fewer experts. Used only by that tool.

options.name: tf_overlap_sets
options.label: Overlap tool: expert weight sets
options.doc: Diagnostics for the overlap measuring tool: how many distinct expert weight sets the routed experts read (1 to 384, built-in 384, the full 1.94 GB a layer streams). 1 or 8 keep them in the GPU cache so the time excludes the weight stream. Used only by that tool.

options.name: tf_round_log
options.label: Nemotron: round log
options.doc: Diagnostics for the Nemotron model family: logs each round. Not used by the DeepSeek engine.
options.label: Rocinante proxy idle sleep
options.doc: A proxy with no send scheduled for this many microseconds sleeps in the kernel until the host schedules the next. 0 keeps it napping on the doorbell instead. On by default at 2000: idle proxies sleep in the kernel (measured with outputs equal, the speed level and the first request after idle at 138 ms against 135). Set it to 0 to keep them napping on the doorbell.
options.label: Rocinante proxy housekeeping interval
options.doc: An idle Rocinante proxy reads the clock for its watchdog and collects finished work every this many turns (built-in 16).
options.label: Allow a test-instrument build to serve
options.doc: Diagnostics: only a test build with extra instruments reads this. Set to 1 it lets that build serve; without it the build refuses to start. A release build ignores it.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_signal
options.label: Rocinante arrival signal
options.doc: How Rocinante tells a receiver a part has arrived: by default atomic (an RDMA atomic add, which InfiniBand orders after the data: the guaranteed arrival) or write (an 8-byte RDMA write of a generation word). A card without atomics: left unset, Rocinante sends the write and says why in a warning; set to atomic, the start refuses by name. Every node must agree.
options.label: Rocinante nap deadline
options.doc: The longest a Rocinante proxy naps, in microseconds (built-in 100, held between 10 and 2,500). The doorbell write ends a nap by itself, so this only bounds a nap no write ended.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_wait
options.label: Rocinante waits inside the network card
options.doc: On by default: Rocinante's queue pairs are loaded in advance and wait inside the card for the GPU's doorbell write, so no proxy thread runs. Set 0 for the fallback proxy threads. If the card route cannot run, an unset value falls back with the reason logged; every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_ring_wait
options.label: Decode rings wait in the card
options.doc: On by default: each decode exchange's transfers are queued in the card in advance and wait there for the GPU's doorbell, so no proxy thread polls. Set 0 for the proxy threads. Needs the generation-word signalling; if something is missing the rings fall back with the reason logged. Every node must agree.

options.name: tensorfold_admin_policy
options.label: Per-key request limits file
options.doc: A JSON file giving each API key label its allowed request extras: custom headers, batch-only, and the thinking-budget and wait-time limits and defaults. Unset, those extras in a request are ignored. Read at start and again when keys are reloaded.

options.name: tf_goal_mode
options.doc: Which goal the controller watches. Off watches nothing. Decode first keeps each decoding user at the decode goal and lets the prompt have the rest above its floor. Prefill first keeps the prompt at the prefill goal and lets decoders have the rest above theirs. Alert only: the controller measures and reports, it never changes the rounds after a prompt step.
options.label: Goal mode

options.name: tf_goal_decode_tps
options.doc: Tokens a second each decoding user should see, drafts included. One stream alone makes about 64 on prose (measured), so 100 on prose is unreachable and the report says so.
options.label: Decode goal per user

options.name: tf_goal_prefill_tps
options.doc: Prompt tokens a second over all prompts filling. One 4,096-row step alone does about 6,500 (measured), so more than that is unreachable.
options.label: Prefill goal

options.name: tf_goal_n_cap
options.doc: The most rounds after a prompt step the controller will ever want: a decode goal that needs more is reported short.
options.label: Most rounds a goal may ask for

options.name: tf_ds_kv_vmm
options.label: KV pool in virtual memory
options.doc: Places the KV pool's cache planes in a CUDA virtual-memory reservation instead of ordinary device allocations: each plane has a fixed stretch of address space sized for the largest pool the Spark could hold, and only the front of it is backed by memory. Same pool size, same bytes, same layout of planes; the planes' addresses never change, which is what lets a later live resize keep every captured graph. Costs up to one allocation granule (2 MiB) of rounding per plane. On when set to anything but 0, on every rank (a follower: the environment).

options.name: tf_ds_roci_stagger_lanes
options.label: Passes in flight
options.doc: How many consecutive whole prompt passes run at once when the stagger is on: 2 (the pair) or 3 (a third pass on a third Rocinante lane). Measured on the four Sparks (a cold ~147K-token prompt): no gain at 3 (6,433 tok/s against 6,491-6,507 at 2, inside the noise), compute time a pass +2.7 % (three streams co-running stretch every kernel; idle unchanged at 39.7 ms), and about 5.5 GiB less free memory a Spark: keep 2. Needs TF_DS_ROCI_STAGGER=1 and passes of at most 10,240 rows; a Spark under the memory floor refuses 3 by name. Replies unchanged.

options.name: tf_ds_add2_vec
options.label: Four-wide owner-sum add
options.doc: The owner sums' bf16 add (about 84 launches a 4,096-row pass, reading the transport's pages) runs four elements a thread with 16-byte loads. The same fp32 add and rounding, so the bytes are unchanged (replay: every output byte equal to the scalar kernel's in every page type); it cuts the time the add spends on the arena's locked pages. On unless 0.

options.name: tf_ds_pack_epilogue
options.label: Expert pack codes in gate/up
options.doc: Gate/up writes the expert pack's FP8 codes and scales into the transport's send region itself, so the separate quantizing launch does not run (about 5 to 6 ms a 4,096-row pass, estimated, not measured). Needs TF_DS_MMA_SF_EXACT (not beside TF_DS_GEMM_R2 or TF_DS_GEMM_W16) and the pack as codes; where a rank cannot run it the start says why and gate/up and the quantizing launch run as before, on every rank. Replies unchanged by contract.

options.name: tf_ds_attn_twin
options.label: Sparse attention kernel variant
options.doc: Which build of the packed-latent sparse attention the calls of TF_DS_ATTN_U (prompt chunks) and TF_DS_ATTN_U_DECODE (decode rounds) launch. u is the standard kernel (the FP4 latents unpacked in hardware). w reads the latents' scale bytes in the code bytes' own layout and unpacks the code bytes where they sit in their registers: 136 fewer instructions and 4 fewer barriers a key block. x is w, reading the next block's pick indices a block ahead and, in the fused attention epilogue, prefetching the next block's rows into the GPU's first-level cache (opt-in until a timing shows it faster than z). z is w, and in a decode round it also prefetches the picked rows into the GPU cache before it waits for the kernel before. All of them give the same bytes (the kernels replay compares them); It runs z unless set (a bit-identical speed change is on by default); u, w or x selects another. Needs TF_DS_ATTN_U or TF_DS_ATTN_U_DECODE and the kernel kit's extra set; without them, or with a kit that lacks the kernel, the engine runs u and says so in an 'off' line of the speed report. A value other than u, w, x or z refuses the start by name. The fused attention epilogue (TF_DS_ATTN_EPI_FUSED) has its own switch, TF_DS_ATTN_EPI_TWIN; this one does not move it.

options.name: tf_ds_rope_w
options.label: RoPE on 32-bit pairs
options.doc: RoPE on the attention heads reads and writes each (even, odd) pair of bf16 values as one 32-bit word, one 128-bit access for four pairs where it made eight 16-bit ones. On by default (a bit-identical speed change); 0 turns it off. The same bytes as the standard kernel (the kernels replay compares them with NaN, infinity and minus zero planted). Needs the kernel kit's extra set; a kit without the kernel keeps the standard RoPE kernel and says so in an 'off' line of the speed report.

options.name: tf_ds_dec_group2
options.label: Faster expert grouping in decode
options.doc: Makes a decode round group its routed rows by expert with a parallel scan instead of one thread block counting entry by entry. A speed option, on unless set to 0; the grouping it writes is byte for byte the same, so replies do not change. Each rank reads its own setting.

options.name: tf_ds_merge_d
options.label: Wider decode attention merge
options.doc: Makes a decode round merge its attention's partial results with several thread blocks a row instead of one: 3 (the default) gives each block 16 columns of the head (32 blocks), 1 gives 128, 2 gives 64, 0 keeps the single block. A speed option that needs the kernel kit's extra set (without it the engine says so at the start and keeps the single block; a kit without the 16-column variant runs 128 columns and says so); replies do not change. Each rank reads its own setting.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_next_early
options.label: L2 prefetch: next layer, earlier
options.doc: Records the next layer's L2 prefetch (its attention mix and input linears) behind the experts' gate / up instead of behind down, so it runs beside the network exchange and down and its weights are in L2 earlier. Measured on the Sparks' decode capture: the dense linears run 2x faster (wq_a + wkv 30 -> 15 us) when their prefetch had 80 us of lead, and 96 % of the standard placement's prefetches are still running when the consumer starts. On by default (the prefetch writes nothing); 2D decode windows on the native kernels only; 0 places it behind down. Replies unchanged.

options.name: tf_ds_window_once
options.label: Window indices uploaded once per chunk
options.doc: On by default (set to 0 to upload them in every layer): a prompt chunk uploads its window gather indices, window low position and ring-write indices once for the whole chunk instead of in every layer. The bytes the engine computes are unchanged. The gain has not been measured on the Sparks.

options.name: tf_ds_attn_epi_fused
options.label: Epilogue in the attention kernel
options.doc: A prompt chunk's attention epilogue (the inverse rotary embedding and the quantization for the next projection) runs in the final store of the attention kernel from the kernel kit's extra set, so the attention output is never written; the same codes and scales. Needs the attention epilogue on; layers with packed latents take it only with the hardware-unpack attention. On by default; without the kit's kernel the engine says so at the start and runs the separate epilogue. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_hc_2s
options.label: Four streams in one mix program
