options.doc: A prompt chunk's hyper-connection mix on the transport's two bf16 blocks runs one program for the four streams of a column block (from the kernel kit's extra set), so the previous streams and sums are read once for the four; the same bytes. On by default; without the kit's kernel the engine says so at the start and keeps the one-stream program. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_qgate_canary
options.label: Quality gate's canary (changes replies)
options.doc: Diagnostics for the quality gate only, never a serving setting: 1 the output head reads its rows after one more FP8 rounding step (the gate's ruler); 2 layer 0's MoE partials take one more FP8 step before their gather; 3 they move one fp32 ulp away from zero (a reduction order's size). A known small change the gate must detect; it changes replies. Every node must use the same setting (a start whose nodes differ is refused). Leave unset.

options.name: tf_ds_draft_vocab
options.label: Drafter on a short vocabulary list
options.doc: The drafter proposes from a list of 32,768 token ids (8,192 on each node: the model's special tokens and the ids most frequent in the project's own text) instead of the whole vocabulary, so its output head reads about a sixteenth of the bytes and its Markov steps score a sixteenth of the columns. A draft is only a proposal the model checks, so replies are the model's own whatever the list holds; what the list changes is which tokens get proposed. A guard on rank 0 counts the committed tokens that fall outside the list and returns to the whole head while more than 2% of the last 4,096 do. On by default; set it to 0 to turn it off. Needs the four-node layout, TF_DS_DRAFT_HEAD=fp4 and the kernel kit's Markov kernels; where a rank cannot run it the start says so and every rank drafts from the whole head. Every node must agree.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_xlog
options.label: Exchange log (capture matching)
options.doc: Diagnostics, log only: the decode ring's peers kernel records, for each exchange and peer, the sequence and, on the GPU's own clock, when the kernel started, when that peer's words were all in and when the copy-out ended (a ring of 8,192 records in device memory, 256 KiB); each rank writes roci-xlog-rank<R>.txt when its ring closes. Per rank, wait and copy-out are then exact (one clock), and captures from the four ranks pair on the sequence instead of by time. Costs a few stores, two clock reads and one block barrier on each exchange's copy-out when on, nothing when off. Replies unchanged.

options.name: tf_ds_roci_xlog_dir
options.label: Exchange log folder
options.doc: Where TF_DS_ROCI_XLOG writes each rank's roci-xlog-rank<R>.txt when the ring closes; unset: the folder's log directory ($HOME/.cache/dsv41-tensorfold/logs). Created if missing. Only read with TF_DS_ROCI_XLOG=1.

options.name: tf_ds_qkv_plain
options.label: Q norm and window KV, one launch
options.doc: A decode window's q RMSNorm and the window KV's RMSNorm, RoPE and FP8 quant-dequant (two launches on the native kernels) as one launch of the kit's extra set's _q_kv_norm variant without rotations: each program is the code of the kernel it replaces, so the bytes are the same (replay section qkv_plain). On by default; a kit without the variant prints an 'off:' line at the start and keeps the two launches. 0 keeps the two launches.

options.name: tf_ds_nact_log
options.label: Expert count log
options.doc: Diagnostics, log only: every decode launch's grouping appends a record (rows, distinct experts, how many this node owns, whether the shared expert is active) to a 4,096-record device ring, written to nact-rank<R>.txt every 256th call and at close: what a launch's gate/up and down weight bytes are, which no other counter keeps. Off: no launch and no copy. Replies unchanged.

options.name: tf_ds_nact_dir
options.label: Expert count log folder
options.doc: Where TF_DS_NACT_LOG writes nact-rank<R>.txt; unset: the folder's log directory ($HOME/.cache/dsv41-tensorfold/logs). Created if missing. Only read with TF_DS_NACT_LOG=1.

options.name: tf_ds_attn_epi_twin
options.label: Fused attention epilogue kernel
options.doc: Which kit kernel the fused prompt attention epilogue (TF_DS_ATTN_EPI_FUSED) launches. ue is the standard kernel (_sparse_attn_part_ue). we runs ue's epilogue after w's mainloop (the latents' scale bytes read in the code bytes' layout, unpacked in place): measured x1.020 on prompts, replies byte-equal. xe is we, reading the next block's pick indices a block ahead and prefetching that block's rows into the GPU's first-level cache: x1.012, below we (its 21 register spills cost more than the prefetch saves). All three give the same bytes (the kernels replay compares them). It runs we unless set (a bit-identical speed change is on by default); a kit without the kernel keeps ue and says so in an 'off' line of the speed report. A value other than ue, we or xe refuses the start by name. Separate from TF_DS_ATTN_TWIN, which picks the decode and unfused calls' kernel.

options.name: tf_ds_l2_chunk_kib
options.label: L2 prefetch: chunk size
options.doc: The size of each bulk prefetch of the L2 prefetch that runs beside the decode exchanges: 8 (the default, as served), or 1, 2, 4, 16 KiB. A wave is 128 chunks, so the memory queue a wave puts ahead of the network card's reads and the staging copies is 128 x the chunk; a smaller chunk with the same rate (the wave period scales with it) leaves a shallower queue. Bit-identical: it touches no value, only when the same cache lines are fetched; replies do not change. Values other than 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 refuse the start. Each rank reads its own setting.

options.name: tf_ds_idx_tpp
options.label: Key tiles per index program
options.doc: How many 64-key tiles one program of a prompt chunk's index score takes in turn. 0 is the standard kernel. 4 uses the kernel kit's tile-looping build: the program reads its rows' queries, head weights and visible lengths once for the four tiles instead of once a tile, and prefetches the next tile's keys into the first-level cache; the same scores, keys and tile maxima (the kernels replay compares them). On by default (4): the kernel time measured on the Spark was 0.958 to 0.980 of the standard kernel's at the 9 shapes of a 4,096-row pass, the same bytes. 0 runs the standard kernel. Only 0 and 4 are built: another value refuses the start by name; a kit without the kernel leaves it off with a line saying why.

options.name: tf_ds_aq_vec
options.label: Four-lane activation quantizer
options.doc: The activation quantizer (the front's input, wo_b's input, the experts' pack, wo_a's input rows) runs four lanes a 32-value group with 16-byte loads instead of a warp a group with 2-byte loads. The same bytes (every output byte equal to the standard kernel's over the prompt pass's shapes and fills with NaN, infinities, zeros and subnormals, kernels replay act_quant; measured on the Spark: 140 of 140 comparisons identical, the big prompt shapes x0.89 of the standard kernel's time, 1,024 rows x0.27 to x0.64), so it is on unless set to 0, which runs the standard kernel for every call. A call that is not bf16 or whose addresses or strides are not aligned runs the standard kernel either way. Any value but 0 or 1 refuses the start.

options.name: tf_ds_woa_merge
options.label: Attention output groups in one launch
options.doc: A prompt chunk's wo_a on its FP8 rows (TF_DS_WOA_W8) runs both groups of a layer as one launch of the bf16-from-FP8 tile kernel (grid z = groups) instead of one launch a group. A group's launch is 256 tiles on 48 SMs, 5.33 waves, so 6 with the last one a third full; one launch over both is 10.67 waves, so 11: about one wave a layer by the wave arithmetic. Each tile runs its group's code unchanged, so the bytes are the group launches' (kernels replay woa_merge). On by default because of the kernel time measured on the Spark: a layer's wo_a took 0.945 of the two launches' time (null 0.998), about 2.1 ms of a 4,096-row pass, the same bytes (the wave estimate of 3.7 to 3.9 ms was high: the merge trims the tail wave, it does not remove it); 0 runs one launch a group. Any value but 0 or 1 refuses the start.

options.name: tf_ds_split64n
options.label: Exact split GEMMs on a 64-column tile
options.doc: With the exact-arithmetic matrix multiplies (TF_DS_MMA_SF_EXACT), a prompt chunk's wkv (512 columns) and wq_a (1,280 columns) run their split GEMMs on a 64 x 64 tile of 128 threads, two blocks an SM, instead of the 64 x 128 tile of 256 threads: their grids are 64 and 160 blocks on 48 SMs. A warp's 32 x 32 tile and every output element's K chain are the same, so the bytes are the 128-column tile's (kernels replay split64n); each rank decides for itself. On by default: at a 4,096-row pass's 1,024 owned rows the 64 x 64 tile takes 21.4 % less kernel time for wkv and 17.9 % less for wq_a (null control 0.0 %, measured on the Spark); 0 runs the 128-column tile.

options.name: tf_ds_yarn_factor
options.label: YaRN factor of the RoPE tables
options.doc: The YaRN factor the kit's RoPE tables were cut for, and with it the positions a stream may reach: 65,536 x the factor (16 = 1,048,576, the checkpoint's own; 32 = 2,097,152, outside what the model was trained on). Unset is the checkpoint's. The kit's rope.json names the factor its tables were cut for; a start whose kit and setting differ, or whose context is past the positions the factor reaches, is refused and says so. Every rank must use the same value; the context (CONTEXT) and the pool follow it.

options.name: tf_ds_pf_t64
options.label: Router GEMM on a 64-row tile
options.doc: The router's bf16 GEMM of a prompt chunk (384 experts, K 5,120; the owned rows) runs on a 64 x 64 tile of 128 threads, two blocks an SM, instead of the 128 x 128 tile of 256 threads: at a 4,096-row pass's 1,024 owned rows its grid is 24 blocks on 48 SMs, half the GPU idle, and 96 on the smaller tile. A warp's MMA chain and every output element's K chain are the same (no split-K), so the bytes are the 128 x 128 tile's (kernels replay pf_t64); each rank decides for itself. Off until the kernel time is measured on the Spark.
